title: Paper Hopper: mini lit review + experiments to try
content:
Snapshot: quick scratchpad for 3 papers + MLOps Summit talk I skimmed. Intention: capture the kernel ideas, jot experiment ideas we could try on Redwood infra, and list concrete small-batch experiments that fit into a 2-week spike. This is messy — notes to self and to Arjun/Maya for pairing.

Top-line takeaways (so I don't forget):
- Small-batch distillation + targeted KV-compression seems promising for reducing memory without large quality loss on retrieval-augmented flows. The gains are workload-dependent; helpful for long-context RAG but less for short prompts.
- Prefix-aware caching (store compressed prefix summaries rather than raw KV) gets large throughput wins when retrievals are semantically redundant.
- Runtime-aware kernel selection (down to per-shard quantization level) is useful: cheaper kernels when sequence length is short; keep high-precision for hot prefixes.

Papers skimmed (note: very quick skims, not deep reads)
1) "Sparse Prefix Distillation for Retrieval-Aware LMs" (arXiv XXXX.YYYY)
   - 1-sentence: distill long prefix influence into compact sparse tokens that are appended to KV cache to emulate long context at lower cost.
   - interesting bits: teacher uses full context; student learns a sparse set of synthetic prefix embeddings. Teacher-student training uses contrastive loss to preserve next-token logits.
   - things I liked: avoids storing full token-level KV; can be applied post-hoc to an existing model (nice for Redwood's private customers).
   - caveats: eval mostly on synthetic long-text datasets; unclear robustness across retrieval noise.
   - experiments to try on Redwood: take a 7B open model we host, synthesize student prefixes for our top-10 retrieval patterns from production traces, measure perplexity and pipeline latency when serving with prefix-cache vs full-kv cache. Measure token-cost delta in both hosted and dedicated.

2) "KV Compression via Structured Low-Rank + Product Quant" (NeurIPS workshop paper, 2028)
   - 1-sentence: combine block low-rank approximations across attention keys + per-block product quantization to compress KV cache with controlled reconstruction error.
   - interesting bits: adaptive block sizes by token type (e.g., code vs natural language), and a small retraining step to reduce downstream generation degradation.
   - implementation notes: core computation requires efficient gather/scatter when decompressing at attention time — could be integrated into our kernel-selection logic so decompression is fused with matmul to avoid extra memory traffic.
   - experiments to try: prototype a decompression-fused attention kernel in our serving runtime (local spike), measure additional CPU/GPU cycles vs memory savings. Run across different seq lengths (512, 2048, 8192).

3) "Robust RAG with Cache-Aware Retriever" (ICLR demo talk summary)
   - 1-sentence: make retriever aware of downstream cache strategy; retrieve documents that maximize unique useful context given what's already cached.
   - interesting bits: simple scoring modification (penalize overlap with cached prefixes), small gains in ROUGE/EM in demos.
   - why it matters: prevents wasted bandwidth moving similar chunks into cache; synergizes well with prefix-compression idea.
   - experiments: instrument a mini retriever that knows current cache fingerprint; compare retrieval choices and downstream answer quality on closed-book QA traces.

MLOps Summit 2029 notes (talk: "Operationalizing KV compression")
- Speaker: Dr. L. Moreno (company) described 3-stage rollout: offline compression, canary in low-traffic shards, auto-fallback to uncompressed KV on quality regression at route level.
- Practical ops tip: keep a delta-monitor on a small curated eval set (100 prompts) as a canary metric — cheaper than full A/B but catches big regressions fast.
- Safety net: keep per-request signature so we can deterministically replay compressed vs uncompressed path to reproduce issues.

Concrete small experiments (2-week spike plan)
- Spike 1 (week 1): Data + distillation
  - pick 50k production retrieval contexts (anonymized), run teacher->student distillation to create 1–8 'prefix tokens' per context using the sparse-prefix paper's objective.
  - metric: validation perplexity and generation logits distance on held-out 5k contexts.
  - success criteria: <= 3% logit distance increase and prefix size < 10% of original KV size.
- Spike 2 (week 2): Runtime + serving integration
  - implement a decompression-fused attention primitive in the runtime (prototype CPU fallback if GPU kernel is heavy).
  - run end-to-end latency & cost for top-2 real workloads with and without compression on hosted tier.
  - monitor: tail latency (p95/p99), token throughput, cost-per-token estimate.

Operational considerations / risks
- Reproducibility: must keep deterministic mapping from original KV -> compressed representation for debugging. Save compression seeds + small recovery tool.
- Quality regression: require per-route canaries + automatic rollback; tie to rollout system in console so SRE/product can control.
- Data sensitivity: compressed representations still derived from customer context; check if KMS/HSM policy needs extra controls for Private deployments.

Open questions (for discussion)
- How brittle are distilled prefixes across query distribution shift? Do we need periodic re-distillation (weekly)?
- Does compression increase hallucination risk when retrieval is noisy? Could we add a small verification rerank step?
- Cost tradeoffs: what's the CPU vs GPU cost of decompression at inference — is it strictly beneficial on GPUs with large memory but limited compute?

Quick TODOs and follow-ups
- [ ] Chat with Arjun about snapshotting top retrieval contexts to build student prefixes (ACTIONS: Arjun to prepare anonymized dump by Mon).
- [ ] Open GH spike repo skeleton and add poc kernel benchmark (owner: me).
- [ ] Add 100-canary prompts to the canary suite and wire an alert for >2% generation divergence.
- [ ] Draft short proposal for Product about Dedicated customers (privacy implications + optional toggle).
